25.0.s.en: (1) Israel's fornication and fall into idolatry

25.0.0.en: Shittim: the word Shittim means acacia trees, and this word was applied to the place where the people camped because of the availability of a large number of acacia trees in this place (map 5). Although the people were very near the Promised Land and nothing separated them from it but the river Jordan, they fell into a great evil, for they fell into fornication with the pagan daughters of Moab and thereby violated all the divine covenants and commandments. The Book of Revelation mentions that behind this terrible stumbling block that brought the people down was Balaam, for he is the one who suggested this to Balak out of greed for money, since he failed to obtain Balak's gifts because God commanded him to bless the people and not curse them, so he resorted to this stratagem to obtain Balak's gifts and told him that if the people of Israel committed fornication and worshiped idols, their God would forsake them (see Rev 2:14), making it easy for Balak to fight and defeat them. And this is what actually happened, for the women of the Moabites whom Balak sent seduced the men of Israel.

25.1.0.en: And because sin drags another sin behind it, and lust, when it possesses a man, takes away his will and his insight, the people fell into the next sin, which is the sin of idolatry and bowing down and offering incense to idols, in open defiance of God, their Savior and Redeemer and the One who brought them out of the land of Egypt. For the Moabite women lured the men of the children of Israel just as happened with King Solomon (1 Kgs 11), and as a kind of courtesy and participation the men bowed down and worshiped the idols.

25.2.0.en: The matter developed from mere bowing down to something more, for it became faith and love toward the god of the Moabites, and the people replaced their God with an image and an idol to which they sacrifice, from which they ask, and in whose powers they trust, namely the god Peor, so God's anger was kindled against His ungrateful people, who insulted Him and insulted His holy name and His glory and honor.

25.3.0.en: The Lord spoke with Moses and commanded him to take "the heads of the people" and to hang them on a tree after killing them, and that their bodies be left "before the sun," that is, before the eyes of all the people, so that they might be a lesson to the rest of the people and the sin might stop and God's anger against them also stop, so that they would not be exposed to the greater punishment. So Moses gathered the judges of the people and commanded them to kill "every one his men," that is, everyone of his tribe who had worshiped Baal-peor and seduced others to worship him.

25.3.1.en: Sin is exceedingly sinful, and a man sinks into it gradually, and when he makes light of God's kindness and patience and does not repent after his fall, the punishment is great and severe. For God does not tolerate evil, so beware, my brother, of being careless, and do not say that this sin is small and that one is great, for the first leads to the second, and the wages of both is death.

25.4.s.en: (2) The zeal of Phinehas the son of Eleazar

25.4.0.en: The people took refuge at the tent of meeting, as they were deeply affected by God's anger and the killing and hanging of some of their men, and also in seeking His mercies, since God, besides the killing of those fornicators and worshipers of Baal, struck the people with the plague, which took thousands of them (v. 9). And while the people were weeping over their sin and asking for pardon, a man of the tribe of Simeon appeared with a Midianite woman, in open defiance of Moses and all the feelings of the people, and to add a new provocation to God by his carelessness and his insolence against the holiness of the house of God, for he passed before it in pride and arrogance.

25.5.0.en: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron was a priest, and his father Eleazar was high priest after the death of Aaron, and when Phinehas saw the sight of this Israelite man with the woman, he was jealous with great zeal for the house of the Lord and the glory of the name of the God of Israel, and took a spear, most likely from one of the men around him, and went in after the man into the tent, "the pavilion," and thrust both the man and the woman through the belly with the spear and killed them, and when God saw what Phinehas had done, He lifted the plague from Israel.

25.6.0.en: The number of those who died in the plague was twenty-four thousand, and we notice that St. Paul mentioned this very incident in (1 Cor 10:8) with a difference in the number, for he said that they were twenty-three thousand ... so is there a difference ...?! In answer to this difference we say:

25.6.1.en: a) The first opinion: that the total number of those killed was twenty-four thousand, of whom twenty-three thousand were in one day, as St. Paul mentioned in the text of the verse, and therefore the following thousand could have been on another day.

25.6.2.en: b) The second opinion: that the true number who died in the plague is a figure between twenty-three thousand and twenty-four thousand, and that the Book of Numbers used rounding up and St. Paul used rounding down to the lower whole number.

25.7.0.en: Perhaps some felt that this conduct of Phinehas was excessive, but the situation was a contempt on the part of the Israelite man, the companion of the Midianite woman, that would stir up laxity among the people, so God declared His pleasure and delight in what His priest Phinehas did, and declared this to Moses. And He makes clear that this conduct of Phinehas represents what God wanted, for he was jealous with a jealousy like that of the heart of God and acted according to His pleasure, and God declares to Moses that because of this conduct the rest of the people were not consumed, and therefore He commanded Moses to tell Phinehas that God gives him a special blessing and a covenant of peace. And the expression "covenant of peace" means a firm covenant for his peace.

25.8.0.en: As a reward for Phinehas, God gives His promise and blessing to him and to his descendants after him that his priesthood would be an everlasting priesthood, in return for what he did and how he removed God's wrath from His people by punishing the sinner.

25.8.1.en: And the expression "everlasting priesthood" means so long as the Levitical priesthood remains, which would of course end with the coming of Christ and the cessation of animal sacrifices. And every covenant to which the inspired Word applied the description everlasting means a covenant that remains in force as long as man is careful to keep it, but if man sins and neglects his life, he by this conduct annuls this covenant and even deserves punishment. And the verse in its spiritual meaning also makes clear to us that God never forgets the labor, or the true witness, or the zeal of a man offered for the glory of His name, for God keeps His covenant and His kindnesses to those who love His holy name.

25.9.0.en: In these two verses the name of the Hebrew man and the Midianite woman is mentioned, so as Phinehas was honored and his name and his work mentioned, so also God mentions the name of the one who sinned and was killed, and the remarkable thing is that the sinful man was a chief of one of the clans of the Simeonites and had a high standing among his tribe, but God and His priest, who was responsible for carrying out His commandments, wants to teach us that there is no partiality in the execution of His judgment. It is to be noted that the woman was also the daughter of a chief of one of the clans of the Midianites, who was like a ruler or a mayor, for example. And this shows Phinehas' courage in his obedience to God's command, not fearing the position of the man or the woman.

25.9.1.en: Beware of laxity or sin even if you are a servant or a deacon or a leader, because no person is above error, and although God forgives all sinners when they repent, He punishes the careless and the one who treats sin as permissible.

25.10.0.en: After the end of the plague, God commands Moses to fight the Midianites, and God makes clear the reason for the war against them: they are the authors of the plot and the snare that they set for the people of the children of Israel, and of their being brought down into fornication and bowing down to Baal-peor, and among them was the fornicating woman "Cozbi," the daughter of one of the chiefs of their clans, whom Phinehas the priest killed when he was jealous with zeal for the Lord. And indeed Israel fought Midian and prevailed over them, and the details of that are in (ch. 31). It is to be noted here that there was an alliance of the Midianites, among whom was "Cozbi," with the Moabites, who sent daughters to cause the children of Israel to stumble and fall into fornication, for some tribes of the Midianites lived beside the Moabites, and therefore God commanded Moses to fight the Midianites, in addition to the fact that He had fought the Moabites also.

25.10.1.en: The second numbering of the people and the numbering of the Levites

26.0.0.en: After the incident of the plague and the death of about twenty-four thousand, God commanded Moses, together with Eleazar the priest, to take the sum and number of all the males of the people of the children of Israel who were more than twenty years old, who are those able to bear arms and go to war. And the expression "after the house of their fathers" means according to their tribes and clans, except the tribe of Levi, because it is set apart for the service of the house of God.

26.0.1.en: This is the second numbering of the people, while the first was 38 years before, at the beginning of their going out to the wilderness of Sinai, and it is the one mentioned in (Ex 30:11, 38:36, and also ch. 1).

26.1.0.en: The plains of Moab: the place where the people were settled at that time, which is the plain extending east of the river Jordan opposite Jericho, which lies across on the western side of the Jordan (map 5). Moses and Eleazar spoke with the people of what God had commanded them, as He had commanded them 38 years before in the first numbering after their coming out of the land of Egypt and their encamping in the wilderness.

26.2.0.en: In verses (5-51) is a listing of each tribe and the number of its males, and so that the dear reader may not be wearied, we shall summarize all that came in these verses in a table that shows the figure and also shows the difference in the numbers between the first numbering (ch. 2) and this second count, but we must note the following observations:

26.2.1.en: 1- The command was to number all the tribes except the tribe of Levi, whom God chose for guarding the tabernacle, and therefore its men do not enter the wars but devote themselves to the important spiritual task to which God appointed them.

26.2.2.en: 2- This numbering was a psychological preparation of the people for the series of wars they would enter, as we say now, a kind of military mobilization.

26.2.3.en: 3- Knowing the number of each tribe also helps in dividing the lands in a way that suits each tribe.

26.2.4.en: 4- An affirmation of God's true promise, for despite the destruction of most of the generation that came out of the land of Egypt and the hardship of life in the wilderness, God blessed their number, and they became almost as they had been, apart from a slight decrease.

26.2.5.en: 5- In (v. 9) the name "Dathan and Abiram" of the tribe of Reuben is mentioned, and God indicated that they are the ones who took part in the rebellion and murmuring of Korah, an indication that a deed is usually tied to its doer and disgraces him if it is a bad deed, and the reputation of this person remains tied to his error; and likewise in (v. 10) he mentions the rebellion and its punishment and the number of those who died in it.

26.2.6.en: 6- In (v. 51) he mentions the total number of the people after the numbering, and it was (601,730), six hundred thousand, one thousand, seven hundred and thirty, and this number is less than the first numbering by one thousand eight hundred and twenty (1,820), which is a very small difference.

26.2.7.en: Name of the tribe, first count, second count, sign of increase or decrease. Reuben 46500 43730 - Simeon 59300 22200 - Gad 45650 40500 - Judah 74600 76500 + Issachar 54400 64300 + Zebulun 57400 60500 + Ephraim 40500 32500 - Manasseh 32200 52700 + Benjamin 35400 45600 + Dan 62700 64400 + Asher 41500 53400 + Naphtali 53400 45400 -

26.2.8.en: If it was necessary to number the conscripts for war before invading the land of Canaan, then you should prepare yourself for spiritual warfare, and discipline your senses and arm yourself with the weapons of the Spirit, which are prayer and the Holy Bible, relying on the sacraments of the Church, which guarantee you victory however much Satan schemes to destroy you.

26.3.s.en: (2) The way of dividing the land

26.3.0.en: Although Moses himself would not divide the land but his successor and disciple Joshua, God directs His speech to Moses because he was still the leader of the people. As for the manner of division that God explained to Moses, that the division be according to numbers, that is, the tribe that has the greater number of males, as in the count, possesses a larger share, and the reverse is true. And the wisdom of God in that is to be noted, so that each individual in the end takes an equal share.

26.4.0.en: So that no disputes might occur among the tribes, God commanded Moses that the land be divided into twelve parts and lots be cast to determine for each tribe a part of the land. And after the land is determined, the survey division of the land is made according to the number of males in each tribe.. so if the number of the tribe is less than the land it took, a part is cut from it and given to the tribe whose number exceeds the land it possessed. It is to be noted that the actual division among the tribes was carried out by Joshua (Josh 15-19).

26.4.1.en: God is just in dividing the land so that every person takes an equal share with the rest. So imitate Him and be just in your judgments with others, and do not show partiality to anyone because you were swayed by his manner of speech or out of fear of him or for any personal purposes that benefit you. And know that the just God looks upon you in all your works and words.

26.5.0.en: As God did before, He does here also, and the Levites are numbered alone, separately, and not with the count of the people. First he mentions the heads of the great clans of the Levites, who are the sons of Levi, to whom the subsidiary clans afterward are ascribed, as we shall see, and the three great clans were the Gershonites, the Kohathites and the Merarites" (ch. 2).

26.6.0.en: The three great clans branched into other clans, and he mentions their names also.

26.6.1.en: a) The Libnites: named for Libni the son of Gershon.

26.6.2.en: b) The Hebronites: named for Hebron the son of Kohath.

26.6.3.en: c) The Mahlites: named for Mahli the son of Merari.

26.6.4.en: d) The Mushites: named for Mushi (Ex 6:19). e) The Korathites: named for Korah the son of Izhar the son of Kohath (Ex 6:18, 21). It is to be noted that the other names of the sons of Levi mentioned in (Ex 6:16-25) are not mentioned here because they were joined to the clans of their brothers because of their small numbers.

26.7.0.en: The inspired Word mentions the name "Amram" and his wife "Jochebed" of the whole tribe of Levi because of their importance, since they were the parents of Moses and Aaron and Miriam.

26.8.0.en: Likewise the inspired Word is concerned to mention Aaron and his descendants because to him alone belongs the priesthood, so it mentions the names of his four sons, who are "Nadab," "Abihu," "Eleazar," and "Ithamar," and it also mentions that none of his sons remained a priest except Eleazar and Ithamar, and the reason for that is the death of both Nadab and Abihu by the wrath of the Lord when they dared to offer strange fire on the altar (Lev 10).

26.9.0.en: As for the total number of the Levites counted, it was twenty-three thousand from the age of a month old, and not like the rest of the tribes whose numbering began from the age of war, which is twenty years, and we notice two things:

26.9.1.en: 1- That their number increased by one thousand males over the first count in the wilderness.

26.9.2.en: 2- That God reminds them that they do not possess land, for the land is for the tribes, but the tithes are theirs.

26.10.0.en: After mentioning the number of the Levites, the discourse concludes that this is the total number of the people and the Levites that was counted before the people entered the land and took possession of their portions.

26.11.0.en: God repeats to us His true word, for He said that because of their much murmuring and their fear of entering the land (ch. 14), none of them would enter the new land. And the verse comes here to confirm to us that what God said indeed happened and the punishment was carried out, so none would enter the land except Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who encouraged the people and praised the Lord and the right hand of His power (see ch. 14).

26.11.1.en: God's promises are true, for when He promised that the sons would enter and the fathers who rebelled against Him and refused to enter the Promised Land would die, now He fulfills His promise and the sons enter. So be assured that God fulfills His promises to you and keeps you as long as you are obedient to His commandments.

26.11.2.en: The daughters of Zelophehad and Joshua as successor to Moses
